name: Point of sale
summary: One bonded order at the counter: buyer and seller, no processor in between.
description: The simplest trade Figaro secures: a buyer and a seller resolve a purchase directly. Both lock a stake worth more than the deal, so honoring it is the only profitable move — no card network, no payment processor, no chargeback department. The buyer picks how the goods change hands (on-site, pickup) at checkout; one signature resolves it.

faq.question: How does a walk-in pay at the counter?
faq.answer: With a wallet app on their phone. They open your page, pick the item, and commit; you hand it over; they resolve on the spot. Their phone is the card reader, and nobody sits between you.

faq.question: What does the buyer need?
faq.answer: A wallet, a little ETH for gas, and the token you price in, enough for the item and their own bond of twice the price. A buyer without a wallet cannot use this assembly.

faq.question: What do I put up, and when am I paid?
faq.answer: A bond of twice the price, refunded whole when the buyer resolves, in the same transaction that pays you. The buyer's bond is refunded at the same moment.

faq.question: What if the buyer walks off without resolving?
faq.answer: Nothing moves. Their bond, twice the price, stays locked with yours. They keep the item and are out of pocket by the price; you are out the item and your bond. Hand over after they commit, and resolve before they leave; the assembly is built for the two steps to happen at the counter.
